items.title: The prime divisors where a meromorphic section is not integral form a locally finite set
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a locally Noetherian integral X, an invertible module L and a regular meromorphic section s, both the set of prime divisors Z whose generic point satisfies s not in L_xi and the set of prime divisors with ord_{Z,L}(s) nonzero are locally finite in X (source lines 6758-6773). The proof finds a nonempty open U over which s corresponds to a section of L generating L, observes that any prime divisor occurring in either set must be an irreducible component of the complement of U, and invokes local finiteness of the components of a closed subset.
